title: As He was and Always will
content:
Our town was quiet, we kept to ourselves and didn't care about the world outside. In some cases, ignorance is bliss. We got very few visitors, and neither of them stayed longer than a month in our quaint little town. Until he came drifting.

By this point he'd been here for some time. I owned the hotel where he lived, he was checked into room thirteen. Even after all this time, he didn't talk to anyone, aside from shop clerks and me, when he wanted some maintenance done. I thought he was weird, he talked about how a yellow sign led him here when he first came to town. He was in all aspects of the word, a misanthrope.

That assumption quickly changed at the fifth anniversary of the hotel. Although no one from town frequented it, it was still useful to travellers and drifters. I invited the man, but I didn't expect him to come. However, while I was walking around the lobby, greeting friends and family when James called me over, waving at me from the open bar.

"Man, have you met this guy? He's awesome." James said with excitement lingering in his voice.

"Yeah of course, he lives here." I answered, and paused to think. "Though I didn't take him as a social butterfly." I should have known better.

As the evening shifted to night, the herd of party goers thinned. I had gotten to know the man, and enjoyed his company. I should have known why he was as he was. James was drunk, so he offered to let him sleep on his couch for the night. As they too disappeared into the hallway, I went to my room and slept.

As morning came and the sun shone through the clouds, I got up, noticing that James' car was gone. Brushing my teeth, I turned on the television. I flipped through the channels when the news caught my attention. Eight people had vanished from their homes, all that was left was an identical letter. I don't remember the contents of the letter, but it was something about black suns. My toothbrush dropped to the floor as I ran to room thirteen, going to check on the man.

I knocked furiously, rattling the doorknob as i felt something dark coming from the far wall. I heard a liquid dripping onto the floor, rhythmically. After no answer, I opened the door with my key. As I entered the room, I sensed it was unnaturally quiet and empty. I felt something dark, damp and wrong. Eyes glued to my back, like a force calling. Maybe God...? No, something much more sinister.

As I came to my senses I saw 8 exsanguinated corpses rotting in a corner, a figure cloaked in yellow robes, doused in red, watching them. It was him. "Welcome to my home, the services you provided were not comfortable to me, so i started redecorating. Do you like it?" He said, his voice twisting my mind and soul. And then I saw it, a ninth body, hanging on a pole, blood dripping and pooling beneath his feet. It was James, he was a victim. The man started explaining, how he was not a man. He was not a god. He only was, and always will. I didn't understand, I should have understood.

As I tried to run, my body did not listen, it gave up. My mind still wanted to fight but... maybe I didn't want to. I unchained James from his bindings. As his body fell to the ground, I tied myself up onto the post, readying myself for crucifixion. Next came nothing, before it, came nothing, and I was never a part of anything.

Today I stand in Carcosa, ruled by the king dressed in yellow. Our king, adorned in crown of bone. Our king, who is skeletal remains. My king who rules over Carcosa. Carcosa where the stars are blackened with void that overtook emptiness; where its two suns rise and decay every day. Carcosa where i stand forever, as I always have and will, serving him who always was and will. The King in Yellow.
author: Ornithos
